turns.doctor_question: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Well, Dr. Smith, I... I suppose I’m here because my family insisted, and my friends, too, though honestly I don’t see why I’m the one sitting in this chair when they’re the ones who need to come clean. You see, I came in because they keep pushing these bank papers in my face—stacks of them, highlighted and everything—trying to tell me they prove nothing was taken from me. But I know better. I’ve known for over a year now, clear as day, that they are hiding my money. And it’s not just a little bit, it’s... it’s everything. 

And the lengths they go to! They try to cover it up with all these elaborate excuses. Like, suddenly there are all these "unexpected bills" they have to pay, or they’re talking about "fundraisers" for things I’ve never even heard of, or they’re planning these trips and acting like it’s perfectly normal. But I see right through it. I see exactly what they’re doing. They’re using all of that to launder my money, to hide what they’ve stolen right under my nose. 

So, yes, they brought me here because I won't let it go. I can't let it go! I have to keep confronting them, every single day if I have to, every time they bring up another fake bill or another trip. I have to keep pushing until they finally admit what they’ve done and tell the truth. Because the truth is right there, no matter how many pieces of paper they wave at me.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed, unyielding belief that their family and friends are stealing and laundering their money, despite being shown contradictory evidence (bank papers).

top_partial.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

turns.doctor_question: Aside from the concerns about your money, have you been experiencing any unusual sensory perceptions, such as hearing voices when no one else is around or seeing things that others cannot see?
turns.patient_response:
Voices? Like... imaginary voices? No. No, absolutely not. I mean, I know exactly why you're asking me that. They probably put you up to it, didn't they? They want you to think I'm crazy, that I'm sitting around hearing things that aren't there, or seeing ghosts or shadows or whatever it is people like that see. But my mind is perfectly clear, Dr. Smith. 

I don't see things that aren't there. I see exactly what *is* there. And I don't hear voices in my empty room, I hear *them*. I hear my sister whispering on her cell phone out in the hallway when she thinks I'm asleep. She does this thing where she cups her hand over the receiver, you know, using that low, hushed voice, talking about "deposits" and "booking the flights." I hear real things. Real conversations they try to hide from me. 

So no, no voices. Just the sound of my own family lying to my face. It’s honestly insulting that they would even try to make it seem like I’m hallucinating or losing my grip, because if you just look at the way they act, the way they avoid my eyes when I ask about the bank statements... you don't need to hear imaginary voices to know what's going on. You just need to pay attention, which is exactly what I do, every single minute of the day. I watch them, I listen to them—the real them, not some made-up voice. I don't have anything wrong with my eyes or my ears. They work just fine. Maybe too fine for their liking, since I catch them in their lies all the time.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses fixed, paranoid beliefs that their family is lying, plotting against them, stealing their money, and trying to convince the doctor they are crazy.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly denies hearing imaginary voices or seeing things that are not there.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any changes in your physical health, your ability to remember things, or any new medical conditions that have developed around the time you started noticing these issues with your money?
turns.patient_response:
Physical health? Medical conditions? No, no, look at me. I'm fine. I don't have any sickness or anything like that. I haven't been to a regular doctor in... well, I don't even know how long, because I just don't get sick. I mean, my body works fine. I eat fine, I sleep... well, I sleep when I can, you know, when I'm not having to stay up and keep an ear out for what they're plotting next. But no, there's nothing wrong with my body at all. 

And my memory? Oh, my memory is sharp. It’s a steel trap, Dr. Smith. Honestly, I think that’s what makes them so mad! They probably told you my memory was going, didn't they? They probably sat out in the waiting room and said, "Oh, she's forgetting things, she's confused, she doesn't remember where her money went." But I'm not confused at all. I remember every single detail. I remember exactly what the balance was on my savings account on October 14th last year, and I remember exactly what it said on that fake printout they tried to shove in my face yesterday morning. The numbers don't match. 

I remember everything. I remember the exact look on my sister's face when she realized I knew what she was doing. It was a Tuesday, it was raining, and she was wearing that ugly yellow sweater she bought for one of her so-called "fundraisers"—which, by the way, I remember she said was for a dog shelter, but she doesn't even like dogs! She's allergic! So no, my memory is perfect. It's better than perfect. If I had a bad memory, they would have gotten away with all of this by now. They could have just swept it under the rug. 

They're just fishing for excuses, trying to find some medical reason to explain away the fact that I caught them red-handed. They want you to find a disease so they can say, "See? She's just sick." But there is no medical reason. I don't have brain damage, I don't have some new physical disease. I just have a family full of thieves, and a really, really good memory that won't let them get away with it.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses clear persecutory delusions, believing her family is plotting against her, faking bank documents, and stealing her money.
symptom_reasoning.S031: The patient explicitly denies any memory issues, insisting her memory is 'sharp,' 'perfect,' and that she remembers every detail.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel that anyone outside of your immediate family, such as your neighbors, bank employees, or even strangers in public, is also involved in this situation with your money?
turns.patient_response:
Strangers? Like... like the people at the bank? No. No, why would they care about me? I mean, think about it. It's not them. I go into the bank sometimes, the one down on Main Street, and the tellers... they just look at their computers. They don't know me from anyone else. They just print out whatever fake numbers my family already put in the system. The bank people are just punching keys, you know? They probably don't even realize they're handing me forged papers because my sister is so good at covering her tracks. 

It's not some... some giant plot with the whole town, Dr. Smith. I'm not crazy, that would be ridiculous. No, it's just the people who actually have access. The people who are supposed to be looking out for me. That's what makes it so awful! A stranger on the street, or... or my neighbor, Mr. Henderson, he barely even looks up when he mows his lawn, he doesn't care about my savings. It’s my family. They’re the ones who know my information. They know where I keep my things, they know my birthday, my passwords... because I used to trust them. 

And they use that! They use the fact that we're family to just take whatever they want. Why would they need to pay off a bank manager or get a neighbor involved when my sister can just log into the accounts on her phone while we're sitting right there in the living room? I've seen her do it! I catch the light from her screen reflecting on her glasses, and she's just tapping away, moving my money, and then she looks up and asks what I want for dinner like nothing happened. Just completely cold. 

So no, I'm not pointing fingers at the mailman or the grocery store clerk or people who have nothing to do with it. I don't need to. I know exactly who the thieves are. They're my own flesh and blood, they're the ones who brought me here today to try and shut me up, and I'm not gonna stop until they admit what they did.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed, persecutory belief that their family members are stealing their money and manipulating their bank accounts.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any significant changes in your daily routine, such as losing interest in your hobbies or spending much less time with friends and people outside of your family compared to how you were a year or two ago?
turns.patient_response:
Losing interest? Me? No, I haven't lost interest in anything. I still like doing all the exact same things I used to do a year ago. It's not me who changed, Dr. Smith, it's them. They're the ones pushing me out, trying to isolate me so I don't have anyone to talk to about what they're doing. Because I keep bringing up the money, you see. I won't just let it go, and they hate that. 

So now, suddenly, my own relatives absolutely refuse to help me with my bills. They used to help me sort them out, you know, sit at the kitchen table and go over the envelopes with me because I don't have a job right now and the late fees and all the due dates get confusing. But now? If I even hold up a water bill, my sister just rolls her eyes and walks right out the front door. My aunt won't even answer the phone if it's near the end of the month. They avoid helping me entirely because they know if we sit down and look at the bills together, we have to look at the bank accounts to pay them, and they don't want to answer my questions about where the cash went. They know I'll point right to the screen and say, "Where is the rest of it?" So they just leave me to drown in the paperwork.

And it's not just my family, it's my friends, too. They've all been talking to my sister, I know they have, because they've completely stopped including me in things. Like the fundraisers! I used to always help out with those, setting up the folding chairs or making signs, but now they don't even tell me when they're happening. I have to find out after the fact. And travel plans... well, you can just forget about that. A couple of the girls I've known since middle school went down to Florida last month, and I didn't even know they were going until I saw the pictures on my phone. They used to invite me on every single trip. We used to go everywhere together. 

But because I started telling them about the missing deposits, you know, just trying to warn them about how my family operates and what was being stolen from me, they just cut me off. They probably think I'm gonna ask them for money to make up for what my sister took, or maybe my sister got to them first and told them some big lie about how I'm acting crazy so they shouldn't bring me around. So yeah, my daily routine has changed a lot, but only because I'm being boxed out of my own life just for telling the truth about my own money. They want me sitting alone in my room, quiet. But I'm not going to be quiet.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient exhibits persecutory delusions, firmly believing that her family is stealing her money and conspiring with her friends to isolate her so she cannot expose them.
symptom_reasoning.S025: The patient explicitly denies losing interest in her hobbies or activities, stating she still likes doing all the exact same things she used to do.
